DATA-GROUNDED HYPOTHESIS (3400–3000 BCE):

Over 3400–3000 BCE, the relative abundance of monuments (MonumentCount) and of axes/celts (AxesCelts) — treated in the supplied framework as social and economic capital, respectively — co-varies strongly (Pearson r ≈ +0.87 on the five 100-year grid points; +0.93 on the interpolated series) and both spike sharply at ~3200 BCE (MonumentCount to +0.91, AxesCelts to +2.60 in Z-scores) before falling back. This monument–axes peak does NOT track the prestige-weapon symbols, which stay essentially flat (HatchetSword ≈ -0.43 throughout; Dagger constant at -0.58). Instead it coincides with the one symbolic-capital element that actually moves in-window — house size — which declines steeply from a +2.05 Z-score peak at 3400 BCE to about 0 by 3100–3000 BCE (R² ≈ 0.78 for that decline).

PROPOSED RELATIONSHIP: As symbolic-capital investment in the domestic domain (house size) declines, monument building and axe/celt (prestige-goods) production spike — consistent with a reallocation of social energy from domestic to monumental/ritual and prestige-goods domains. This reallocation occurs during a period of declining landscape openness (Belau+Woserin pollen PC1 MEAN falls from ~+0.08 to -1.86, R² ≈ 0.81) and declining demographic density (kde_all_mean falls ~31%; growth rates g_all_mean are negative throughout) — i.e., a concentration of symbolic/economic investment despite declining demographic pressure. Supporting this: house size is positively associated with both openness (r ≈ +0.67) and demographic density (r ≈ +0.95), whereas monument count and axes/celts are negatively associated with demographic density (r ≈ -0.44 / -0.40).

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: (1) the ~3200 BCE monument+axes peak did NOT coincide with the house-size decline (e.g., house size also peaked at 3200); (2) monuments and axes/celts did not move together (no co-movement); (3) landscape openness and/or demographic density were rising rather than falling during the spike; or (4) the flat prestige-weapon symbols (HatchetSword/Dagger) showed a comparable spike, which would implicate weapon-based symbolic capital instead of domestic/house-size capital.

CAVEATS: all variables are Z-scores (relative abundance, not literal counts); the five-point correlations are directional/low-power (n=5) and the 401-point interpolated correlations are autocorrelated, so no statistical significance is claimed; the 3200 BCE spike is present in the raw (observed) 100-yr values, not an interpolation artifact; the economic-vs-social-capital labeling of AxesCelts/MonumentCount is the supplied interpretive lens, not a property of the data.

payload.workflow: Loaded 3 CSVs (time_series_data.csv annual CE -4100..-500; capital.csv 100-yr BCE 4300..500, comma decimals, group=MN in window; pollen file CE -4785..-702, comma decimals). Mapped German capital columns to English names (data-verified by identical 5-pt values). Extracted the inclusive 3400-3000 BCE window (CE -3400..-3000; calBP 4950-5350). Primary analysis on the 5 RAW 100-yr grid points (3400,3300,3200,3100,3000); interpolated/smoothed series used only for trend/correlation sensitivity. Computed: (1) 5-pt window table with core vars + pollen MEAN/SMOOTH_100y + kde/g context; (2) per-variable delta & peak/trough; (3) linear trend slopes & R2 (5-pt primary + 401-pt interpolated); (4) 5-pt Pearson matrix (directional, n=5); (5) 401-pt interpolated Pearson matrix (autocorrelation caveat); (6) openness/demographic trend read. Produced a data-grounded natural-language hypothesis with falsification conditions.
